title: 2025 CEMC Gauss (Grade 8) Problems/Problem 25
text:
Problem[edit]

The list 11, 12, 14, 23, 31, 44, 45, 46, 56, 64, 67, 74 can be arranged so that the units digit of each number matches the tens digit of the number that follows it. For example, 12, 23, 31, 11, 14, 44, 45, 56, 67, 74, 46, 64 is one such arrangement. How many such arrangements of the given list are possible?

Hint[edit]

Use this information and try to solve the problem again.

We see that the number 1 appears in the tens place three times but in the ones place two times, thus the first number must have 1 in the tens place. Then we also see that 4 appears in the tens place three times and in the ones place four times, thus we also know that the last number must have 4 in the ones place.

Solution (Brute-Force)[edit]

Using the information given by the hint and knowing the fact that the highest possible answer is 36 we can just brute-force this question. Which is what we will be doing.
